To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) a realm is an abstract data type that is used to represent spatial data and (2) ROSE is a spatial algebra defined on top of a realm.

(a) the use of realms as a geometric domain for spatial data types solves the problems of numerical robustness, topological correctness, and geometric consistency, and (b) the ROSE algebra, defined on top of a realm, has very nice algebraic and implementation properties.

the use of realms as geometric domains in database systems offers a general and robust solution to the representation of geometric objects, and that ROSE is a fully general spatial algebra defined in terms of realms and cooperating with database systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the definition of a spatial data model and a spatial query language, both of which are independent of a particular DMBS.
the development of an algebra that meets the requirements of (1)-(5) and is suitable for integration into a DBMS data model.

the development of a general algebra for spatial data types, based on the concept of realms, that is fully general, has formally defined semantics, is defined in terms of a finite representation, offers facilities to enforce geometric correctness of spatial objects, and can be integrated with any DBMS data model and query system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ROSE is the first spatial algebra that meets the above requirements.
ROSE is an algebra for the definition of spatial data types in database systems, that is, it is an algebra for defining the semantics of spatial data types and for defining operations on them.
ROSE provides an elegant solution to the problem of representing spatial data and spatial operations in a database system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a general algebra for spatial data types that is fully general, has formally defined semantics, and offers a framework to enforce geometric consistency.
ROSE offers a powerful, general, yet simple spatial data type system that can be integrated into any DBMS data model and query languages.

we have defined a new algebraic data model for spatial data types, and that this model has been integrated into a DMBS data and query model, thus providing a fully general and consistent framework for spatial databases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the realm-based spatial data type concept is very powerful and flexible, and can be applied in a wide variety of database systems.
the realm-based spatial data model provides a powerful and flexible approach to the integration of spatial data types into a DBMS.

a spatial algebra can be designed in such a way that it is (1) fully general, (2) formally defined, and (3) defined in terms of a finite geometric domain that is independent of a particular DMBS data model, and yet (4) interacts with any DMBS data model in a uniform way.
